# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

| Version | Supported |
| ------- | --------- |
| 3.0.x   | Yes       |
| Earlier | No        |

## Reporting a Vulnerability

If you discover a security vulnerability in kicad-happy, please report it privately via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/aklofas/kicad-happy/security/advisories/new).

Do not open a public issue for security vulnerabilities.

## Scope

The analysis scripts (`analyze_schematic.py`, `analyze_pcb.py`, `analyze_gerbers.py`) parse untrusted KiCad files. Bugs that could cause code execution, path traversal, or information disclosure when parsing a malicious file are in scope.

The scripts are read-only by design — they never modify input files. The BOM management scripts write KiCad symbol properties when run; `--dry-run` previews the change without writing.

## What each input is trusted to do

Nothing in a KiCad file, a project config, a cached model or a downloaded file is executed as code by the analyzers, except a cached SPICE model when you set `spice.trust_project_models` (below). The tools do run a few programs on your machine and make network requests; the table says what each kind of input can and cannot do. Code locations are in `skills/`.

| Input | What the code does with it | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Your own KiCad files (`.kicad_sch`, `.kicad_pcb`, `.kicad_pro`, `.kicad_dru`, legacy `.sch`) | The S-expression files are parsed by the stdlib reader; `.kicad_pro` is read as JSON. Never executed. The analyzers do not modify them. With neither `--output` nor `--analysis-dir`, the schematic, PCB and EMC analyzers still create `./analysis` (or `analysis.output_dir` from `.kicad-happy.json`) and write `capability_mode.json` there; the thermal, Gerber and cross-analysis CLIs do the same in `./analysis`, and with `--output` they write it beside the output file. `bom_manager.py` writes symbol properties when you run it (`--dry-run` previews). | `kicad/scripts/kicad_core/sexp.py:99` (`parse`), `:106` (`parse_file`) |
| A public repository you did not write | Same parser. A sub-sheet is opened wherever the parent sheet names it, after project text variables are expanded, and nothing checks that it stays inside the project folder: an absolute or `../` path is followed. Nesting deeper than Python's recursion limit stops the run with a `RecursionError`. Analyze untrusted repositories as an unprivileged user. | `kicad/scripts/schematic/reader.py:1328-1333`, `kicad/scripts/kicad_core/project.py:278` (`expand_sheet_file`) |
| `.kicad-happy.json` | Read from the project folder and each parent folder, with `~/.kicad-happy.json` as the lowest layer. It sets analysis options (power rails, design intent, suppressions, BOM and output settings). `analysis.output_dir` may be an absolute or `../` path, so a repository you did not write can make the analyzers create that folder and a `capability_mode.json` in it. In the EMC and thermal analyzers a suppression marks a finding `suppressed` and never removes it. It cannot switch on the two trust opt-ins below: those are read from `~/.kicad-happy.json` only. | `kicad/scripts/project_config.py:108` (`_discover_config_paths`), `:519` (`apply_suppressions`); `kicad/scripts/kicad_core/project.py:126` (`load_user_config`) |
| `datasheets.allow_private_hosts` | Read from `~/.kicad-happy.json` only, and only the JSON value `true` counts. When set, a datasheet URL may point at a private, loopback or link-local address, and the browser fallback and a `requests` older than 2.32.2 may be used, since nothing is pinned. The http/https, no-credentials and host-shape checks, the redirect checks and the size and time limits still apply. | `datasheets/distributor_core/download.py:209` (`_allow_private_hosts`), `:168` (`_checked`) |
| Downloaded datasheets | Only http/https URLs whose host resolves to public addresses are fetched; an IPv6 address that embeds a private IPv4 (mapped, NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-compatible) is refused. Every redirect is checked the same way (at most 5). By default a download stops at 50 MB or 120 s (`--max-download-mb`, `--download-timeout`; the browser fallback checks the size from `Content-Length` or after fetching), and a file is kept only if it starts with `%PDF`. Each connection goes to the address that was checked: `requests` from 2.32.2 through an adapter, `urllib` through a pinned connect; an older `requests` is not used. Through a proxy the host is resolved again when the connection opens. The browser fallback resolves each host itself, so it runs only with `datasheets.allow_private_hosts`, and its requests are still checked and fetched by the policy handler. PDFs are not parsed in Python: text comes from `pdftotext` (a 10 s or 30 s timeout; in the Deep Review quote check a 30 s timeout leaves the quote graded partial) or a raw ASCII scan. Extracted text is shown to the agent; treat it as data, not instructions. | `download.py:144` (`_address_problem`), `:161` (`url_problem`), `:285` (`_pinned_create_connection`), `:428` (`download_pdf`), `:684` (`_PinnedAdapter`), `:731` (`_CheckedRedirectHandler`), `:844` (`_policy_route`); limits `:31-35`; `distributor_core/verify.py:126` (`_extract_pdf_text`); `kicad/review/scripts/deep_review_gate.py:472` (`check_datasheet`) |
| Extraction caches (`datasheets/extracted/*.json`) | Read without following symlinks, size-capped at 10 MB, JSON objects only; a linked `datasheets/` or `extracted/` folder found from the project is refused (a directory you name explicitly is not checked). A cache in a repository you did not write is taken as the datasheet's facts and can change datasheet-backed findings. | `datasheets/datasheet_types/cache_reader.py:54-97` (`read_regular_bytes`, `read_json_object`), `:99` (`safe_extract_dir`) |
| Cached or project SPICE models (`spice/models/`) | A cached model is pasted into the generated netlist only if every line is a model-library card (`.subckt`, `.ends`, `.model`, `.param`, `.func`, `.global`), an element line or a comment, plus at most one final `.end`, which is dropped. Any other dot-card, any `.inc`/`.lib` include, a control block, a `shell` or `source` line, or a `file=` parameter anywhere makes the model skipped with a diagnostic; the file is left alone. A linked or oversized model file is refused. `spice.trust_project_models`, read from `~/.kicad-happy.json` only and only as `true`, pastes cached models verbatim. `run_external_deck.py` runs the deck you name as written. | `spice/scripts/spice_model_cache.py:181-226` (`model_text_problem`), `:229` (`model_for_bench`), `:363-376` (`ModelOptions`), `:418-431`; `spice/scripts/simulate_subcircuits.py:657-665`; `spice/scripts/run_external_deck.py:209` |
| Programs on your machine (`ngspice`, LTspice, Xyce, PSpice, `pdftotext`, `pdfinfo`, `gh`) | Looked up by name, never from the project folder. On Windows only absolute PATH entries are searched, because Windows would otherwise try the current directory first. Elsewhere the lookup is `shutil.which` on your PATH. `LTSPICE_PATH` and `PSPICE_PATH` name a simulator explicitly. | `kicad/scripts/kicad_core/executables.py:11-27`; `spice/scripts/spice_simulator.py:215-224`, `:573-587` |
| Distributor API responses (DigiKey, Mouser, LCSC, element14) | Parsed as JSON. A datasheet URL from a response goes through the download policy above. The Mouser product-page scrape fetches the response's `ProductDetailUrl` through the same policy (public addresses, checked redirects, 4 MB and 30 s limits), and the datasheet link it finds goes through the PDF download policy. | `digikey/scripts/provider_digikey.py:287`, `:362`; `mouser/scripts/provider_mouser.py:107-127` (`scrape_product_page`); `datasheets/distributor_core/download.py:807` (`fetch_page_text`) |
